title: Elimination of Time-in-Grade
pass_4_primary_concern: The main record gap is the thin empirical support for removing TIG and the limited explanation of how agencies will replace the time gate with a consistent internal standard.
pass_5_concise_why: The proposal is coherent, but it still needs a stronger explanation of why TIG can be removed without weakening merit-based screening or creating uneven agency practice.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: Agencies may replace a single governmentwide promotion gate with inconsistent local criteria unless OPM explains how merit protection will be maintained.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The notice says TIG is unnecessary, but the record does not quantify how often TIG blocks qualified employees or how often abuse would occur without it.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The available record does not quantify how many qualified employees TIG currently blocks or how often agencies would overpromote without it.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for data, cohort comparisons, or agency examples showing that TIG is actually the problem the proposal says it is.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule removes a uniform time gate but does not provide a governmentwide safeguard, safe harbor, or calibration framework that would keep local promotion criteria consistent.

evidence.section: II. Reasons for Proposed Elimination / Other Regulatory Changes
evidence.quote_or_absence: The available record does not explain what shared safeguard or safe-harbor framework will keep agency criteria consistent after TIG is removed.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask OPM to spell out the replacement guardrails, example standards, or oversight checklists that will keep local discretion from drifting.
